chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Secretive charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord.'

key_terms.تُطْفِئُ: Extinguishes — uses the metaphor of quenching or putting out a fire to describe how the act of giving cancels divine displeasure
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ السِّرِّ: Secretive charity — voluntary almsgiving given privately, hidden from others to maintain sincerity
key_terms.غَضَبَ الرَّبِّ: The anger of the Lord — divine displeasure caused by sin; the hadith implies that sincere charity appeases God's displeasure with the giver's transgressions

ai.seo_question: Does giving charity in secret extinguish God's anger according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Baqir from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), declares that giving charity in secret has the power to extinguish the Lord's anger. The concept of 'sadaqat al-sirr' (secretive charity) was especially prized in early Islamic ethics because it ensured sincerity and freedom from ostentation — when giving is hidden from all except God, it demonstrates true devotion rather than a desire for social approval. For the original audience of the Imams' followers in the early Islamic period, this teaching reinforced the virtue of sincere, hidden acts of worship over public displays of piety.
